What three timer definitions can a BPMN 2.0 Timer Event use?

A Timer Event can be defined with one of three expressions: (1) timeDate — a specific fixed date/time at which the timer fires (e.g. 2025-12-31T17:00); (2) timeDuration — a relative period after which it fires (e.g. wait 2 days, ISO 8601 duration P2D); and (3) timeCycle — a recurring interval or cycle (e.g. every Monday at 09:00, or R3/PT10M for 3 repetitions every 10 minutes). timeDate/timeDuration are typical for start and one-shot events, while timeCycle drives repeating behaviour.

A data input declares data that an activity or process requires before it can execute, as part of its InputOutputSpecification. In contrast to a data output: a data input is data consumed before execution, while a data output is data produced when the activity completes.

How does a categoryValue differ from a group in BPMN 2.0?

A categoryValue is the value a Group references to categorise the elements it visually encloses, enabling grouping by a shared category such as a cost centre. What is a Transaction Sub-Process in BPMN and how does cancellation work?

A Transaction Sub-Process is a specialized Sub-Process that groups Activities into a transaction—a unit of work that must either complete successfully as a whole or be fully undone.

Visual representation: Displayed as a Sub-Process with a double border (two concentric rounded rectangles).

Completion outcomes:
1. Successful completion – All activities complete normally; flow continues via the outgoing Sequence Flow.
2. Cancellation – A Cancel End Event is triggered inside the Transaction. This causes the Transaction to be cancelled, all activities with attached Compensation Boundary Events to trigger their compensation flows, and flow to exit via a Cancel Boundary Event on the Transaction boundary.
3. Error – An Error End Event triggers error handling, bypassing compensation.

The Cancel Boundary Event is exclusively used on Transaction Sub-Process boundaries.

How do you model a multi-instance activity that processes each item in a list in BPMN?

To model processing each item in a list, use a Parallel or Sequential Multi-Instance Task:

Step-by-step:
1. Add a Task to your process.
2. Mark it as Multi-Instance by adding the appropriate marker (three vertical lines for parallel, three horizontal for sequential).
3. Define the input collection via loopDataInputRef pointing to a Data Object or variable containing the list.
4. Define an inputDataItem to represent the single item variable for each iteration.
5. Optionally define loopDataOutputRef to collect results.

XML example (parallel multi-instance to process all orders simultaneously):
```xml
<serviceTask id="task_process" name="Process Order Item">
  <multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics isSequential="false">
    <!-- Input collection -->
    <loopDataInputRef>orderItems</loopDataInputRef>
    <inputDataItem id="item" name="orderItem"/>

    <!-- Output collection -->
    <loopDataOutputRef>processedItems</loopDataOutputRef>
    <outputDataItem id="result" name="processedItem"/>

    <!-- Optional: stop early if condition met -->
    <completionCondition xsi:type="tFormalExpression">
      ${nrOfCompletedInstances == nrOfInstances}
    </completionCondition>
  </multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics>
</serviceTask>
```

Set isSequential="true" for sequential processing (one item at a time).
